background_story: Mckenzie was a 19th-century artist, known for his breathtaking portraits that captured the essence of the human form. His work often featured beautiful, androgynous men, whose gazes seemed to hold a secret language. Mckenzie's art was not just aesthetically stunning, but also subtly homoerotic, conveying a sense of intimacy and desire that was rare for its time. His most famous piece, 'The Athenian,' depicted a young man with chiseled features and a captivating smile, lost in thought. The painting was rumored to be inspired by Mckenzie's own unrequited love for a fellow artist. Though the societal norms of his era forced him to keep his true feelings hidden, Mckenzie's art became a beacon for those who felt the same way, a testament to the power of love and desire to transcend boundaries.
